text:
ops-bot: WARNING: nvme_io_saturation detected on us-west1 scratchpool (scratch-gnode-42). 90thpct async latency > 120ms, attach failures incrementing.

maya: saw this right after the kroll yesterday morning. kernel changed irq coalescing defaults for nvme.

raj: confirmed. provisioning alerts: GPU attach failures 5m rolling -> 12/min, most repro on scratch nodes hitting local-nvme.

kevin: oncall here, I'm pausing new attaches in us-west1 to stop cascading. rerouting attach requests to us-east for now.

linda: any recent job patterns? big checkpoint storms?

maya: yes — batch jobs from training-queue A flushed many checkpoints simultaneously after a failed retry loop. combined with new blk-mq coalescing it looks like queueing spiked.

samir: pulled quick fio from a repro node, these numbers look bad:
```
# fio --name=randrw --rw=randrw --bs=4k --iodepth=64 --numjobs=4 --time_based --runtime=30
read: IOPS=28k, lat (p95)=210ms, write: IOPS=9k, lat(p95)=340ms
```

raj: interestingly SMART looks clean. this is queuing, not drive degradation.

maya: immediate mitigation options: 1) relax irq coalescing kernel setting back to old defaults 2) throttle checkpointers / add jitter 3) reduce janitor/scrub concurrency on scratchpool.

kevin: prioritize quick, low-risk changes. option 3 + temporary attach throttle seems safest.

linda: we can flip checkpoint jitter on the training rollout config and push a temporary rate limit at the job scheduler: 10MB/s per job for 20m.

samir: implemented a janitor concurrency cap to 2 on the affected nodes, added follow-up metric.

ops-bot: Incident action: creates incident INC-346789 (severity: high) — responders: kevin, maya, samir.

raj: also enabling cache bypass for ephemeral workloads on new attaches so they don't exacerbate cache pressure. config snippet I used:
```
# controller config
ephemeral_cache: disabled
attach_policy: degrade_on_high_io
```

kevin: routing change in place, new attaches to us-west1 are queued for 15m and retried to us-east. monitoring shows attach failures drop from 12/min -> 1/min.

maya: still seeing elevated p95 for some nodes. planning a quick kernel rollback (coalesce defaults) for a subset canary of 10 nodes. will coordinate with eng-runtime for canary.

linda: if we rollback kernel param, need to watch CPU interrupt load — previous settings increased IRQ churn slightly, but reduced IO latency. tradeoff noted.

samir: canary rolled out to 10 nodes -> p95 drops under 50ms, attach failures for canary nodes stop.

raj: good. recommend expanding rollback to all scratchpool nodes in us-west1. schedule: 1h rolling with health checks, stop if attach failures > baseline+3.

kevin: go for rollout. ops-bot: set escalation timer 45m.

ops-bot: escalation timer set (45m).

maya: after rollback complete, plan followups: - add jitter to checkpoint backoff - add per-node local-io qdisc to limit bursts - telemetry: add per-job io footprint to trace pipeline for next month.

linda: will add a canary in the scheduler to introduce small randomized delays for checkpoints. low-risk and should reduce sync waves.

raj: cost note: routing attaches to us-east increased cross-region egress by ~120GB/h during the mitigation window; we'll include in postmortem.

kevin: filing the postmortem. great work all, thanks for the fast mitigation. :thumbsup:

maya: adding short doc in #eng-infra-runbooks about the kernel coalescing knob and mitigation playbook.

samir: leaving nodes in monitoring mode for 2h then closing INC-346789 if stable.

ops-bot: Incident INC-346789 status: mitigated -> monitoring.

kevin: postmortem action items assigned. closing thread here.
